items.title: Bischoff na uitschakeling: 'Geen tijd om te rusten, PSV wacht'
items.summary: Clement Bischoff baalt van de uitschakeling van Jong Denemarken, vooral na de sterke start tegen Jong Oranje waarna zijn ploeg hoop had op een stunt. Het heenduel eindigde afgelopen vrijdag nog in een 0-3 zege voor de Nederlandse beloften, maar in Almere waren de Denen met 2-3 te sterk voor Oranje. De middenvelder van NEC kijkt nu vooral vooruit op het duel met PSV van komend weekend.

items.title: Read komt terug op belofte: 'Geen EK was een schande geweest'
items.summary: Aanvoerder Givairo Read blikt terug op de zenuwslopende wedstrijd in Almere tussen Jong Oranje en Jong Denemarken. Het heenduel eindigde afgelopen vrijdag nog in een 0-3 zege voor de Nederlandse beloften, maar zij verloren nu met 2-3 van Jong Denemarken. Na een bewogen kwalificatiecyclus is het Jong Oranje dus gelukt om het EK te halen.

items.title: ‘The game is in danger’: PFA head Maheta Molango on Fifa, Infantino and football’s future
items.summary: At a potentially critical juncture for football, the PFA chief executive talks about the organisation, wider fears in the game and why the Folarin Balogun affair was ‘scandalous’ After five years in charge of the Professional Footballers’ Association, what has Maheta Molango learned? “The game is in danger,” the 43-year-old says. “I’ve learned that the game I loved and led me to first play and then advise and then lead a club and today to lead the PFA, is in danger because it is being forgotten.” In 2026, with football ubiquitous on all platforms, with a World Cup that generated $15bn (£11.4m) in revenue, and with attendances across the English pyramid growing year on year, it may seem hard to imagine forgetting about the game. But Molango’s unique perspective as head of the English players’ union observes a different picture; one where the future of the sport is being determined not by what will maintain its popularity, but what will make the most money. Continue reading...

items.title: ‘I’m entering to win’: Philippe Diallo launches campaign to topple Gianni Infantino
items.summary: French FA chief officially begins bid for Fifa presidency Uefa’s choice hints at ‘support from other continents’ Philippe Diallo, Europe’s candidate to fight Gianni Infantino for the Fifa presidency, said he had received “strong signs of support from other continents” as he launched his campaign in Paris on Tuesday. The French Football Federation president also said he had contacted Kozo Tashima, who announced his candidacy this month, and would try to convince him to “join forces”. Diallo did not indicate whether he would explicitly be asking Tashima to stand aside. “Our approaches are based on the same assessments and the same values,” he said. Continue reading...

items.title: Peter Storey, Arsenal Double winner and England international, dies aged 81
items.summary: Storey made 501 appearances for Arsenal from 1965 He won 19 England caps and finished career at Fulham Arsenal have paid tribute to Peter Storey, a key member of their 1971 Double-winning team, after the death of the former England midfielder at the age of 81. Storey was part of the Bertie Mee team that secured the First Division title and FA Cup in a season that remains one of the most celebrated in Arsenal’s history and played 501 times for the club. That places him eighth on their appearances list. Continue reading...
